title: A number card
description:
Read three whole numbers a, b and c, and print a card about them. For the input `7 -3 10`:

```
+------------------------+
|  Xenon number card     |
+------------------------+
a = 7
b = -3
c = 10
a + b + c = 14
a - b - c = 0
in hex: 0xe
in binary: 00001110
the last one again: 10
```

- The three lines of the frame are one block of data, printed with a single `write` system call, with the dashes made by `times`.
- `in hex:` and `in binary:` show the sum a + b + c; the binary has 8 bits (`print_bin` with `rsi` = 8).
- `the last one again:` is c, printed through a value you kept safe across all the calls before it.
- The program ends with the exit system call and code 0.

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .text
_start:
        call    read_int
        mov     rdi, rax
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

solution.main.asm:
global  _start

SYS_WRITE equ   1
SYS_EXIT equ    60
STDOUT  equ     1

        section .data
frame:  db      "+"
        times 24 db "-"
        db      "+", 10
        db      "|  Xenon number card     |", 10
        db      "+"
        times 24 db "-"
        db      "+", 10
frame_len equ   $ - frame
s_a:    db      "a = ", 0
s_b:    db      "b = ", 0
s_c:    db      "c = ", 0
s_sum:  db      "a + b + c = ", 0
s_diff: db      "a - b - c = ", 0
s_hex:  db      "in hex: ", 0
s_bin:  db      "in binary: ", 0
s_last: db      "the last one again: ", 0

        section .text
_start:
        mov     eax, SYS_WRITE
        mov     edi, STDOUT
        lea     rsi, [rel frame]
        mov     edx, frame_len
        syscall

        call    read_int
        mov     rbx, rax                ; a
        call    read_int
        mov     r12, rax                ; b
        call    read_int
        mov     r13, rax                ; c
        mov     r14, rbx                ; the sum
        add     r14, r12
        add     r14, r13

        lea     rdi, [rel s_a]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, rbx
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        lea     rdi, [rel s_b]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, r12
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        lea     rdi, [rel s_c]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, r13
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        lea     rdi, [rel s_sum]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, r14
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        lea     rdi, [rel s_diff]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, rbx
        sub     rdi, r12
        sub     rdi, r13
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        lea     rdi, [rel s_hex]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, r14
        call    print_hex
        call    print_newline

        lea     rdi, [rel s_bin]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, r14
        mov     esi, 8
        call    print_bin
        call    print_newline

        lea     rdi, [rel s_last]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, r13
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        mov     eax, SYS_EXIT
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: `sub` comes properly in lesson 2.01, and works like `add`: `sub rax, rbx` takes rbx away from rax and keeps the result in rax. So a - b - c is `mov rax, rbx` (a), `sub rax, r12` (b), `sub rax, r13` (c).
Working out a sum must not change the registers holding a, b and c: copy one into `rax` or `rdi` first and add to the copy.
requirements: Keep the three numbers in registers that the routines do not change (`rbx`, `r12` to `r15`).
Name the system call numbers with `equ` (for example `SYS_WRITE equ 1`).
Print the frame with your own `write` system call, and everything else with the routines.
